channel.title: The Hannan Tapes — Updates
channel.description: New shows, re-masters, and fixes in the Hannan live archive.

item.title: Reprocessed Jerry Hannan's solo show at 19 Broadway from March 29, 1999 under the new wor…
item.description: Reprocessed Jerry Hannan's solo show at 19 Broadway from March 29, 1999 under the new workflow (v8), replacing the show's v2 pass — the last remaining show in the archive on the original engine. This was also the show whose Drive noise-reduction export had gone through two separate upload passes months apart, leaving 34 stale duplicate files from the first pass sitting alongside the final corrected export; those were identified by timestamp and cleared before this run. Twenty-nine of the thirty-four tracks needed help beyond plain linear gain: five are handled by the applause-only limiter and sixteen qualify for the sparse-transient-cap mode, reaching the full −20 LUFS target instead of landing quieter. Three tracks' capped moments were confirmed by ear before shipping: “The Wind” (~1% of the track across several short events, e.g. 0:22.95 and 0:39.75), “The Bold Fenian Men” at 1:22.35, and “Hello in There” at 2:31.30 — all legitimate music, not defects. Two suspected digital defects were also checked by ear and confirmed as music, not clicks: “Blind Man” at 3:07.702 and “The Parting Glass” at 2:52.138. One title was restored to the archive's established spelling — “I Need a Lover” to “Hear Me” — and track 30, freshly retitled “Limerick Medley” from the prior catalog's “Some Get Married for Love,” was confirmed correct by ear rather than by cross-reference, since neither title matched anything else in the archive.

item.title: Reprocessed this Mad Hannans set at 4th Street Tavern under the new workflow (v8), replac…
item.description: Reprocessed this Mad Hannans set at 4th Street Tavern under the new workflow (v8), replacing the show's v2 pass. Two songs, “Soundcheck” and “Rocky Road to Dublin,” qualify for the sparse-transient-cap mode and now reach the full −20 LUFS target this way — both cleared automatically, no listen required. Four track titles were restored to the archive's established spelling after the fresh export drifted: “I Need a Lover” to “Hear Me,” “The Kiss - Da Da Da (Slave to an Angel)” to “The Kiss / Da Da Da (Slave to an Angel),” “Shirt” to “Shirt - ABC,” and a dropped closing parenthesis fixed in “Soundcheck (Football Tonight).”

item.title: Reprocessed this Jerry & Sean Hannan set at 19 Broadway under the new workflow (v8), …
item.description: Reprocessed this Jerry & Sean Hannan set at 19 Broadway under the new workflow (v8), replacing the show's v2 pass. Twenty-one of the thirty tracks needed help beyond plain linear gain: eight are handled by the applause-only limiter (crowd noise, not the music, sets the ceiling), and eleven qualify for the sparse-transient-cap mode, reaching the full −20 LUFS target instead of landing quieter. Four tracks' capped moments were confirmed by ear before shipping: “Soundcheck” at 1:50, “Black is the Color” at 1:30 and 2:15, “Good Life” at 2:57.6, and “I've Just Seen a Face” at 2:00 — all legitimate music, not defects. Four track titles were restored to the archive's established spelling after the fresh export drifted: “Never Knew a Woman” to “Woman,” “Seven Drunked Nights” to “Seven Drunken Nights,” “The Kiss - Da Da Da (Slave to an Angel)” to “The Kiss / Da Da Da (Slave to an Angel),” and a stray double space trimmed from “I've Just Seen a Face.”

item.title: Reprocessed this Mad Hannans set at New George's under the new workflow (v8), replacing t…
item.description: Reprocessed this Mad Hannans set at New George's under the new workflow (v8), replacing the show's v2 pass. Six of the fourteen tracks qualified for the sparse-transient-cap mode and now reach the archive's full −20 LUFS target this way instead of landing several dB quieter, most notably “Anna May” (would have landed at −24.1) and “Butter” (would have landed at −22.4). The fresh export used a different track name than the archive's established title for one song — “I Need a Lover” — restored to “Hear Me” rather than overwritten.

item.title: Reprocessed this Mad Hannans set at Sweetwater under the new workflow (v8), replacing the…
item.description: Reprocessed this Mad Hannans set at Sweetwater under the new workflow (v8), replacing the show's v2 corrective-EQ pass — the same restoration EQ, cutting low-mid mud and lifting presence and air on this muddled tape, carries over unchanged. Two songs, “Hear Me” and “Rocky Road to Dublin,” now reach the archive's full −20 LUFS target this way instead of landing several dB quieter; “Far Away Eyes” needed more recovery than the policy's 6 dB ceiling allows, so it lands at −23 LUFS instead of −20 — inaudibly quieter, never over-shaved. The fresh hand-edit export used different track names than the archive's established titles for two songs — “I Need a Lover” and “The Kiss - Da Da Da” — restored to “Hear Me” and “The Kiss / Da Da Da (Slave to an Angel)” rather than overwritten.

item.title: Reprocessed Jerry Hannan's solo show at 19 Broadway from January 15, 2001 under the new w…
item.description: Reprocessed Jerry Hannan's solo show at 19 Broadway from January 15, 2001 under the new workflow (v8), replacing the show's v7 pass. Twenty-one of the set's thirty-one songs qualified for the sparse-transient-cap mode shipped last night — reaching the archive's full −20 LUFS target instead of landing several dB quieter — while “Woman” stayed on the existing applause-only limiter, where a burst of clapping rather than the music sets the ceiling. The fresh hand-edit export used different track names than the archive's established titles for four songs — “State Trooper,” “Everything,” “Four Leaf Clover Inn,” and “Never Knew a Woman” — restored to “Highway Patrolman,” “Everything Reminds Me of You,” “The Barney Stone Blues,” and “Woman” rather than overwritten.

item.title: Reprocessed this Mad Hannans set at Cafe Java again, this time under a new workflow (v8) …
item.description: Reprocessed this Mad Hannans set at Cafe Java again, this time under a new workflow (v8) built for tapes where the mic sat close to the drums: a millisecond-scale true-peak limiter now catches only the sharpest instant of an isolated musical transient — a snare hit, a strum — while the surrounding performance keeps its full, untouched gain, letting more tracks reach the archive's −20 LUFS standard instead of landing several dB quieter. Fifteen of the twenty-two tracks qualified and are now capped this way; “Rocky Road to Dublin / Star of County Down” needed more recovery than the policy's 6 dB ceiling allows, so it lands at −21.6 LUFS instead of −20 — inaudibly quieter, never over-shaved. “Truck” and “Anna May” are untouched by this change: both were already correctly handled by an earlier, unrelated fix that limits only audience applause at a track's edges, not the music. Two titles also picked up small spelling corrections back to the archive's established convention: “ABC (alt version)” and “The Kiss / Da Da Da (Slave to an Angel).”

item.title: Re-normalized this Mad Hannans set at Cafe Java to −20 LUFS on the current audio engineer…
item.description: Re-normalized this Mad Hannans set at Cafe Java to −20 LUFS on the current audio engineering workflow (v7), replacing the show's original v1 pass — the last v1 show in the archive. The fresh hand-edit pass applied noise reduction across the show and corrected the song list: what was catalogued as a single 5:39 track, “Everything Reminds Me of You,” is in fact two songs, now split into separate tracks with the second restored as “Hear Me” — so the show runs 22 tracks rather than 21. “My Dear” has been identified as the song the archive lists elsewhere as “Ride On” and retitled to match, and “Plastic Melons” corrected to “Plastic Lemons.” Elsewhere in the archive, two tracks catalogued as “I Need a Lover” have been corrected to “Hear Me,” the song's real title.

item.title: Brought four more pre-v4 shows up to the current processing engine (v7) — Jerry Hannan at…
item.description: Brought four more pre-v4 shows up to the current processing engine (v7) — Jerry Hannan at 19 Broadway on 1999-05-10, 1999-06-21, 1999-07-19, and 2001-01-15 — replacing early loudnorm-based passes that had occasionally fallen back to dynamic-mode compression instead of true linear gain. All four re-split from fresh hand-edit exports and re-verified against R2.

item.title: Re-normalized all 21 tracks: the show's original v1 processing had silently hit exactly −…
item.description: Re-normalized all 21 tracks: the show's original v1 processing had silently hit exactly −20 LUFS and exactly −1 dBTP on several tracks — the same dynamic-mode fallback bug found in other pre-v4 shows — when tracks like "I Need a Lover" and "You're Pulling Me Leg / The Ted Kennedy Song" in fact needed a target as low as −24.7 LUFS to stay linear. Re-split from a fresh hand-edit pass using the current engine.

item.title: Re-normalized all 30 tracks: the show's original v1 processing used ffmpeg's naive loudno…
item.description: Re-normalized all 30 tracks: the show's original v1 processing used ffmpeg's naive loudnorm, which had silently hit exactly −20 LUFS and exactly −1 dBTP on nearly every track — the signature of the same dynamic-mode fallback bug that flattened Sean Hannan's 1999-11-29 show, since several of these tracks in fact needed a target as low as −28 LUFS to stay linear. Tracks where audience applause — not the music — set the ceiling (Anna May, Luxury of Murder) now get linear gain sized to the music itself, with only the applause gently limited. Also re-split from a corrected label export that fixed a garbled track title and stripped stray junk labels.

item.title: Re-normalized all 21 tracks: a bug in the loudness pipeline had silently switched several…
item.description: Re-normalized all 21 tracks: a bug in the loudness pipeline had silently switched several tracks into dynamic (compressor-like) processing instead of true linear gain, flattening hand-drawn fades and room dynamics. Tracks where audience applause — not the music — was the loudest thing on the tape now get linear gain sized to the music itself, with only the applause gently limited. Track 7, "The Rodeo Song," has some audible clipping baked into the source recording — normalization can't undo that, so it's flagged rather than papered over — using the automated audio engineering workflow with ffmpeg

item.title: Added the Mad Hannans' return to Marin Brewing Co. in Larkspur, April 1, 1999 — the venue…
item.description: Added the Mad Hannans' return to Marin Brewing Co. in Larkspur, April 1, 1999 — the venue's 10th anniversary, one year to the day after their first show there — as 15 individual tracks normalized to −20 LUFS. "Da Da Da (Slave to an Angel)" now opens with its "The Kiss" intro, missing from the 1998 show. Two audience transfers of the tape survive; the tracks come from the cleaner one, with the other kept as an alternate full-show download.

item.title: Added the earliest Mad Hannans show in the archive, April 1, 1998 at Marin Brewing Co. in…
item.description: Added the earliest Mad Hannans show in the archive, April 1, 1998 at Marin Brewing Co. in Larkspur, as 17 individual tracks normalized to −20 LUFS. It's a rough audience recording left without EQ or noise reduction, and "Da Da Da (Slave to an Angel)" still lacks the "The Kiss" intro it later picked up. Includes a Steve Miller cover, "Space Cowboy."

item.title: Recovered 7 more songs from the rougher of the two August 23, 1999 19 Broadway reels and …
item.description: Recovered 7 more songs from the rougher of the two August 23, 1999 19 Broadway reels and added them to the show page as a separate "Part 1 (Distorted)" batch — rough listening in places, but archived rather than lost. Includes an alternate "ABC," another early "Rugburns," and three songs new to the archive: "Troy," "The Kiss," and "Da Da Da (Slave to an Angel)."

item.title: Added the August 23, 1999 solo show at 19 Broadway as 14 individual tracks, normalized to…
item.description: Added the August 23, 1999 solo show at 19 Broadway as 14 individual tracks, normalized to −20 LUFS. The two source reels are mislabeled, so this main set comes from the cleaner of the two. Includes an early version of "Rugburns" and a Steve Poltz cover, "Single Life."

item.title: Added the June 7, 1999 solo show at 19 Broadway as 29 individual tracks, treated with bro…
item.description: Added the June 7, 1999 solo show at 19 Broadway as 29 individual tracks, treated with broadband noise reduction (10dB on the first three tracks, 6dB after, sensitivity 5) across the whole tape before splitting, then normalized to −20 LUFS. Includes the Irish traditional "A Bunch of Thyme" and a birthday singalong for an audience member named Marco.
